what.text: This page follows people displaced inside South Sudan by conflict and violence, counted by IDMC and by UNHCR and shown side by side.
At the end of 2025, IDMC estimated 944894 people in internal displacement, and UNHCR counted 1277527.
Refugees from South Sudan live mainly in Uganda, Sudan and Ethiopia.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of South Sudan from 2011 to 2021 and again in 2025, at war level in 2014.
The groups fighting the government include the SPLM/A - IO, which UCDP also lists in 2025.
Floods and wildfires are the disasters recorded for South Sudan in IDMC's data.

when.text: The main years of displacement in the data are 2014 to 2023, and IDMC recorded the most new displacements from conflict in 2014.
IDMC's figure peaked at 1898699 in 2017 and fell to 944631 by 2024.

how.text: In 2025 IDMC counts 332633 fewer internally displaced people than UNHCR; the figures overlap and are never added.
IDMC's new displacements count movements, not people: someone forced to move twice in a year is counted twice.
The sources don't say where inside South Sudan people moved to.
